page: Amazon Web Services r7a.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by a 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9R14 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of high-speed 5 GHz DDR5 memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks demonstrate strong single-core capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core testing, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics generally fall within the average range, though uncached large-block read-only memory bandwidth is a relative bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25%. Cryptographic and vector operations are supported by hardware-accelerated instruction sets including AVX-512 and AES.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r7a.xlarge offers a dense memory profile relative to its compute footprint, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. It is well-suited for database operations, caching layers such as Redis, text processing, and lightweight web serving.
